newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold, silver track world rally, end up.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold, silver track world rally, end up.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat ends 50 rupees higher at 4,390 rupees on the back of rally in world markets
** Gold biscuit (116.64 gramme) closes 500 rupees higher at 51,300 rupees per piece
** Silver (.999) ends 115 rupees higher at 6,265 rupees

Gold 24 carat closed 50 rupees higher at 4,390 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close o 4,340 rupees on the back of physical and speculative buying following reports of rally in the world market, dealers said.
Limited inflow and hike in the premium on import licence also helped local prices to bounce back after recent losses. Gold was down to 5 year's lowest level last week.
Gold biscuit (116.64 gramme) closed 500 rupees higher at 51,300 rupees per piece after gaining 150 rupees on Wednesday.
"The premium of special licence to import bullion has gone up today to 11.10/11.15 percent from 10.70/10.75 percent," one broker said. It had crashed to 9.60/9.70 percent last week.

Silver (.999) closed 115 rupees higher at 6,265 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,150 rupees amid negligible arrivals while shortage of ready stock and recovery in the world market prompted speculative buying.
Silver was up by 20 rupees per kg on Wednesday but was down by 275 rupees on Tuesday.
The overall market sentiment was firm for both the precious metals at the close of the session.
